📺 You work the deep pools — the rich ones, the far ones. Crab the size of your head. Mussels by the handful. The water is at your ankles. Then your calves. You are getting rich and the tide is getting closer.
📺 First gull-cry. Then the second. The causeway is wet stone now, the pools merging into one rising sheet. Your sack is heavy. The deep pools are still giving. The water is at your knees.
📺 One more pool. The richest one, of course. You fill the sack to bursting. The water is at your thighs and moving like it has somewhere to be. You have somewhere to be too: OUT.
📺 THIRD GULL-CRY. The causeway is going under — white water over black stone, the pools gone, the whole flat drowning in real time. You are on it. The far side is a long, wet run.

📺 You RUN. Water to the knees, then the waist, the sack held high like an offering. The far rocks. Your feet find them. You come out of the water hauling dinner for the whole village, soaked to the soul, grinning like a maniac. The crowd detonates.
